note: Asked after the 21 core questions. Answers never change pillar or overall scores; they produce a separate AI readiness score.

questions.title: AI Use Policy and Ownership
questions.text: How clearly does your organization define acceptable AI use, and who owns it?
questions.help: Covers generative AI, AI-assisted coding and AI agents. Ownership means a named person or team accountable for the policy, not just a document.

options.label: No AI use policy and no owner
Informal guidance or a general policy line, with no clear owner
Written AI use policy with a named owner; the awareness program is consulted
Policy co-owned with security awareness and reviewed on a set schedule
Policy co-owned by security awareness, reviewed with leadership, and updated as tools change

questions.title: AI Tool Visibility
questions.text: How well does your program know which AI tools employees use, sanctioned and unsanctioned?
questions.help: Includes free and personal accounts used for work. Visibility usually comes from DLP, CASB, browser or network telemetry, owned by another team.

options.label: No visibility into which AI tools are used
Anecdotal knowledge from requests and incidents only
Known for sanctioned tools, partial for unsanctioned ones
Regular reporting across sanctioned and unsanctioned tools, by department
Continuous visibility across tools and account types, feeding program priorities

questions.title: AI Guidance Reach
questions.text: Does your AI guidance reach the groups that use AI most, not just the enterprise tenant?
questions.help: Heavy AI use tends to concentrate in a few functions (often legal, sales and marketing, and engineering), and much of it happens outside the sanctioned tool.

options.label: No AI guidance, or none beyond the policy itself
One all-staff message or module for everyone
Guidance targeted to some high-use groups
Role-specific guidance for most high-use groups
Tailored by role for every high-use group, including personal-account use

questions.title: AI-Enabled Social Engineering
questions.text: How well are employees prepared for AI-enabled social engineering, such as deepfake voice and video or AI-written lures?
questions.help: Preparation means a verification habit (for example, calling back on a known number) that employees practice, not only awareness that deepfakes exist.

options.label: Not covered
Mentioned in general awareness content
Covered in content, with a clear verification rule
Practiced in simulations for high-risk roles
Practiced in simulations, with out-of-band verification habits measured

questions.title: Safe AI Use
questions.text: How well are employees trained in safe AI use: what to paste, reviewing output, and granting agent and tool permissions?
questions.help: Covers generative AI, AI-assisted coding and AI agents that act on an employee's behalf.

options.label: Not covered
Policy acknowledgment only
Annual module on safe AI use
Role-specific training covering generative AI and AI-assisted coding
Role-specific and in the workflow, covering generative AI, AI-assisted coding and agents

questions.title: AI Behavior Measurement
questions.text: How does your program measure AI-related behavior?
questions.help: Observed behavior means events such as sensitive data pasted into AI tools or permissions granted to AI apps, not completion or acknowledgment rates.

options.label: Not measured
Policy acknowledgment and training completion only
Some observed behavior, reviewed occasionally
Observed behavior tracked regularly and reported
Observed behavior tracked, trended and used to set program priorities

questions.title: AI Incident Reporting
questions.text: Do employees know how to report AI misuse or an AI mistake, and can the organization investigate it?
questions.help: For example, an employee who pasted customer data into a public AI tool: would they know where to report it, and would someone pick it up?

options.label: No reporting path for AI misuse
Reported informally, if at all
A reporting path exists but is rarely used
A known reporting path that is used, with defined triage
Used regularly, and investigations feed back into training
